about: The Lauda Sion sequence of Saint Thomas Aquinas. It praises Christ present in the Eucharist, expounds transubstantiation, and ends by asking for a share in the banquet of the saints.

seg.tr: Praise, O Zion, your Savior; praise your Leader and Shepherd in hymns and canticles.
Dare as much as you can, for He is greater than all praise, and you cannot praise Him enough.

ex.w017: “Greater” describes the Savior praised in the preceding stanza. The subject and verb are understood: “for He is greater than all praise.”

seg.tr: The theme of special praise, the living and life-giving Bread, is set forth today.
At the table of the holy supper He was given to the company of the twelve brethren; this is not doubted.

a.g: the table of the holy supper
to the company of twelve brethren

seg.tr: Let praise be full and resounding; let the rejoicing of the mind be glad and fitting.

ex.w050: The first two wishes concern praise. In the next two, “it” refers to “the rejoicing of the mind,” named afterward.

seg.tr: For a solemn day is kept, on which the first institution of this table is recalled.

a.g: the first institution of this table is recalled

seg.tr: At this table of the new King, the new Pasch of the new law brings the ancient Passover to an end.

a.g: brings the old Passover to an end

seg.tr: Newness drives away the old, truth drives away the shadow, and light banishes night.
What Christ did at the supper He commanded to be done in remembrance of Himself.

a.g: He commanded this to be done

seg.tr: Taught by sacred precepts, we consecrate bread and wine into the victim of salvation.

a.g: we consecrate into the victim of salvation

seg.tr: A dogma is given to Christians: bread is changed into Flesh, and wine into Blood.
What you do not comprehend or see, a courageous faith confirms beyond the ordinary course of nature.
Beneath different appearances—different only as signs, not in reality—extraordinary realities lie hidden.
The Flesh is food and the Blood is drink; yet Christ remains whole beneath either species.
He is not cut, broken, or divided by the receiver; He is received whole.
One receives, a thousand receive; they receive as much as he, and the One received is not consumed.

a.g: and the One received is not consumed

seg.tr: The good receive and the wicked receive, yet with unequal lot: of life or of destruction.
It is death to the wicked and life to the good; see how unlike is the outcome of an equal reception.
When at last the Sacrament is broken, do not waver, but remember: as much lies beneath the fragment as is covered by the whole.

a.g: When at last the Sacrament is broken
as is covered by the whole

seg.tr: No division is made in the reality; only the sign is broken, whereby neither the state nor the stature of what is signified is diminished.

a.g: No division of the reality is made

seg.tr: Behold the Bread of Angels, made the food of wayfarers; truly the Bread of the children, not to be cast to dogs.
He is foreshadowed in figures: when Isaac is offered, when the paschal lamb is appointed, and when manna is given to the fathers.
Good Shepherd, true Bread, Jesus, have mercy on us. Feed us and guard us; make us behold good things in the land of the living.
You who know and can do all things, who feed us mortals here: make us there Your table companions, fellow heirs, and comrades of the holy citizens. Amen. Alleluia.

a.g: know and can do all things

ex.w284: Latin leaves “us” understood. “Make us” governs the earlier descriptions: Your table companions, fellow heirs and comrades. “Of the holy citizens” describes the fellow heirs and comrades.
